model_annotations.Bulgarian: This chart illustrates the relationship between sparsity rate and perplexity for two different quantization or pruning strategies, labeled "Per-Output" and "Per-Layer." The horizontal axis represents "Sparsity Rate" with categorical labels at 10%, 20%, 30%, 40%, 50%, 60%, 70%, and 80%, arranged in ascending order from left to right. The vertical axis represents "Perplexity" on a logarithmic scale, ranging from approximately 5 to 10³ (1000), with dashed gridlines at 10¹, 10², and 10³. The chart uses grouped bars, with each sparsity rate having two adjacent bars: a blue bar for "Per-Output" (positioned on the left within each group) and an orange bar for "Per-Layer" (positioned on the right). At 10% sparsity, both bars are very short and nearly equal, with values close to approximately 5. At 20% and 30%, the bars remain similarly low, still near 5. At 40%, the values increase slightly to roughly 5–6. At 50%, both bars reach approximately 6–7. At 60%, the bars begin to diverge more noticeably, with Per-Output at approximately 10 and Per-Layer at approximately 12. At 70%, Per-Output reaches approximately 20 and Per-Layer approximately 35–40. At 80%, the bars are tallest, with Per-Output reaching approximately 500–600 and Per-Layer approaching approximately 900–1000. The bars are not sorted independently but follow the natural ascending order of sparsity rates, and the increasing bar heights become dramatically more pronounced at higher sparsity rates due to the logarithmic scale. No bars appear to be visually emphasized through bolding, outlining, or annotation beyond the standard color coding described in the legend.
